learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines of their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; select and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately, and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet the established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Ability and skill to design and carry out experimental investigations, interpret results, and reach conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in their field of specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment, and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in their field of specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Relates the mechanical and physical properties of metals to their composition and heat treatment.

syllabus_topics: Structure of materials (bonding, structures, defects and alloys)
teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, performed individually or in teams
Teacher presentation in class, in participatory lessons, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Practical sessions in workshops and/or laboratories, individually or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical capacity, project involvement/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, presentation, and technical defense

assessment_rules: For individual written and oral tests, recovery is possible through similar tests. For reports on exercises, case studies, and lab practices, the final corrected version of the project report serves as recovery. Project evaluation is continuous, based on meetings with tutors and experts, and feedback is provided a week before final submission to identify improvements. Some project-based assessments (100% weight for specific competencies) do not have separate recovery mechanisms, with the final corrected report serving as the recovery.
